title: Oboe
summary: Limits first: the scale plays 22 to 158 c flat, each note locking onto the third resonance, which the reed's compliance pulls down as pitch squared; the first resonance is +10 to +32 c sharp, and C4 and C5 don't follow. The reed's mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed (a clarinet's mass and damping, another reed's data). There is no tongue or hole vortex loss, and the breath noise row on Bb4, Db4, G5 and Ab5 drives only 10 to 20 kHz on this reed's 0.87 mm duct. A C major scale and Ode to Joy are up, each note its own render at one fixed 7.4 kPa, on fingerings inferred from Table III of Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, the one complete oboe tone-hole table we hold. Bb4 (7 of 15) and Db4 (6 of 14) are graded pages; G5 and Ab5 play an octave down and have no grade; Eb6 has no render because the printed ladder ends at D5.
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; a description gives them this bore and a reed with values partly borrowed from the clarinet, and the posted first renders come from it

flow noise at the reed on Bb4, Db4, G5 and Ab5 (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated), with the card's first bore record, 0.87 mm, as its duct radius, by the clarinet cards' rule. At that radius it drives only 10 to 20 kHz, and the code takes the open-area ratio as 0 where this reed's is about 0.8
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional oboe players are retained as player data

Fingerings chained from Table III's closed and open tones for each hole: inferred, not printed, from C4 to C5 and on the page notes. Where the table prints two rows for a note, the scale takes one and says which; the octave aids, holes 1, 2 and 5, aren't printed and are closed
physics_missing: a measured bore profile and bell flare: only reads from the paper's graphs exist
pad and key heights, undercut geometry and a full fingering chart
a double-reed valve driving this bore (paired reed or the material-modal valve)
a modern specimen: the only complete table is from 1967
A printed pressure for each note: Fuks and Sundberg print note pressures for D4, F4, Bb4, D5 and F5 only, so every note here uses the pages' fixed 7.4 kPa

The scale's tuning. Each note from D4 to B4 plays within 8 c of the third resonance divided by three (hand model, card reed), and the reed's compliance pulls that resonance down as the square of the pitch (Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, eq. 36, the cavity term: -22, -104 and -171 c on C4, A4 and C5 against -23, -106 and -174 on the hand model); the first resonance sits +10 to +32 c sharp. C4 and C5 don't follow that rule. A player's push doesn't fix it (3 mm at the reed end raises the first passive peak 3.0 to 17.1 c). The reed's blade mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, and no oboe reed's are printed: they need the authors or a measured reed
blocked: The paper's bore graphs are read and its tables were transcribed from the page images, but no open source prints an oboe reed's blade mass, stiffness or damping. Needs those from the authors or a measured reed, and a newer measured oboe.
